patch.summary:
Thesis: Overlapping use cases, different tradeoffs — Motion and Trello share buyer workflows; choose based on documented strengths and limits.

Comparison thesis: Overlapping use cases, different tradeoffs. Choose Motion only if your buying job matches “AI calendar + task auto-scheduling (projects, docs, meetings) — Pro AI from $19/seat/mo an” rather than Trello's shape. Choose Trello only if your buying job matches “Lightweight Kanban boards (Atlassian) — Free; Standard from $5/user/mo annual.” rather than Motion's shape. Workflow advantage: Motion leans work-management; Trello leans team-collaboration-work. Trade-off: you gain focus on one product's motion at the cost of the other's adjacent coverage — no universal winner.

Major differences:
- Buyer thesis: Overlapping use cases, different tradeoffs — Motion and Trello share buyer workflows; choose based on documented strengths and limits.
- Positioning: Motion is AI calendar + task auto-scheduling (projects, docs, meetings) — Pro AI from $19/seat/mo annual.; Trello is Lightweight Kanban boards (Atlassian) — Free; Standard from $5/user/mo annual..
- Workflow coverage skew: Motion-leaning work-management vs Trello-leaning team-collaboration-work.
- Researched limits: Motion — Premium $19+ seats vs broader Work OS floors; Trello — Limited planning depth vs Work OS.

Limitations — Motion: Premium $19+ seats vs broader Work OS floors; AI credit caps and top-ups affect TCO; Trello: Limited planning depth vs Work OS; Premium needed for richer views.

Poor-fit cases: Motion is a poor fit when that limitation bites: Premium $19+ seats vs broader Work OS floors · Trello is a poor fit when that limitation bites: Limited planning depth vs Work OS · Avoid Motion if you actually need Trello's motion (Lightweight Kanban boards (Atlassian) — Free; Standard from $5/user/mo annual.)

Neither product has a completed hands-on product test on SoftwareGlimpse — this comparison is research/data-based only.
